translation_notes: sibling of test_invalid_fdo_from_nanopub_network in the same source file; the same conventions were applied so the two translations stay comparable

the 9 graph.add() calls become 2 islands: URIRef('...') -> <...>, RDF.type -> a, SH.x -> sh:x, DCTERMS.conformsTo -> dcterms:conformsTo, FDOF.FAIRDigitalObject -> fdof:FAIRDigitalObject, Literal('Value') -> "Value".

the six profile_graph.add() calls merge into ONE island: `shape` becomes the island-scoped label _:shape and `property_bnode`, used once as the object of sh:property and carrying three properties, becomes an inline [ ... ] property list. The two BNode() calls therefore disappear -- pure term-construction scaffolding that nothing else read.
Literal(1, datatype=XSD.integer) -> "1"^^xsd:integer (kept explicit rather than Turtle's bare 1, to mirror the source's explicit datatype); the terms are identical.
record_graph and profile_graph are function locals, so `graph += g{ }` needs no `global` declaration.
the @patch("nanopub.fdo.validate.requests.get") decorator arguments stay opaque Python strings, as intended: islands do not apply inside strings.

same trade-off as the sibling: `from nanopub.namespaces import FDOF` is dropped and the ontology IRI inlined in `@prefix fdof: <https://w3id.org/fdof/ontology#> .`, so the ldpy file no longer tracks the library's own constant. DCTERMS/RDF/SH/XSD and URIRef/Literal/BNode imports likewise become dead; only `from rdflib import Graph` survives (still needed by the demo harness).

demo harness added identically to both representations: the region is a pytest test that returns nothing and keeps both graphs in locals. The harness wraps MagicMock to capture the two assertion graphs and republishes them at module level for isomorphism comparison; it needs a try/except around `mock.assertion` because MagicMock rejects attribute names starting with 'assert' unless explicitly set. The test's own assertions (is_valid is True, errors == []) run on both sides.

the region's imports of nanopub are left as upstream; the driver puts the corpus checkout of commit 05022dc4bc on sys.path (sys.dont_write_bytecode). requests.get is mocked with the handle metadata, so the JSON-schema-to-SHACL path runs offline through pyshacl; profile_graph is only fixture data on this branch.
